changes.before: Sequential sensor readout records different rows at different instants, so fast lateral motion or rapid camera movement produces a coherent direction-dependent shear: straight structures lean or bend consistently, moving forms skew across their height, and some local detail can remain crisp. A Dutch angle, wide-angle convergence, global warp, or ordinary motion blur cannot substitute.
changes.after: Temporally staggered sensor-row exposures record different image positions at different instants, so fast lateral subject motion or rapid camera movement produces coherent readout-axis shear according to each form's motion relative to the camera. Moving image forms lean or shear while stationary forms relative to a fixed camera retain stable geometry, and some local detail can remain crisp. A Dutch angle, wide-angle convergence, arbitrary warp, or ordinary motion blur cannot substitute.
